For further information and guidance please contact your train company or speak to a member of railway staff.

nrIncident.message:
There is a fault with fault with the signalling system between Berwick-upon-Tweed and Newcastle. This has closed all lines running between this station.
As a result of this issue, trains running between these stations may be cancelled in full, delayed by up to 60 minutes or revised to only run for part of their normal journey.
Please note, some morning services may also be affected following damage to the overhead wires that was sustained in the Drem area yesterday afternoon. Repair work for this issue has now been completed, however, owing to the severity of the issue, some services may still be subject to alterations and cancellations as train crew and units were out of place for the start of service this morning.
If you have an LNER, Lumo or TransPennine Express ticket dated for travel yesterday, Sunday 15 November, and you deferred travel, you will be able to use your ticket to travel today, Monday 16 November, at no extra cost. LNER customers only may also use their tickets on Tuesday 17 and Wednesday 18 November.
Major disruption is expected until 10:00.
There are a number of different options available to help you complete your journey. Please check your whole journey using the National Rail Enquiries journey planner as some of the alternative routes listed below that you can use your ticket on may also be affected by this disruption.
A visual disruption map video is available.
CrossCountry customer advice:
Rail replacement transport been requested to operate between Edinburgh and Newcastle. You will be updated here once this is confirmed.
You may use your ticket to travel on the following services at no extra cost:
• LNER services between Edinburgh and Doncaster
• TransPennine Express services between Edinburgh / Glasgow Central and Manchester Piccadilly / Leeds
• Avanti West Coast services between Edinburgh / Glasgow Central and Birmingham New Street
• Northern services:
• Between Newcastle and Carlisle
• Between York and Preston
You may also use your ticket on the following operators on alternative viable routes if your train is cancelled:
• Northern
• LNER
• TransPennine Express
You do not need to amend your ticket to use it on these services.
If your CrossCountry train is cancelled, you may use your ticket on CrossCountry services operating two hours before or two hours after your cancelled service.
If you decide to travel from a different station due to this disruption and need to return to that station later, you will also be able to use your existing ticket to do this at no extra cost.
Unfortunately, any seat reservations will not be carried over to another train, but coaches B, H and L are the unreserved coaches on CrossCountry services (where available) so please head to them.
LNER customer advice:
Rail replacement services are in operation between Edinburgh and Newcastle.
You may use your ticket to travel on the following services at no extra cost:
• Avanti West Coast between Edinburgh / Glasgow Central, Manchester and London Euston
• CrossCountry between Edinburgh / Newcastle and York, Leeds / Doncaster, Sheffield
• Lumo between Edinburgh and London Kings Cross
• Northern between Carlisle and Newcastle
• TransPennine Express between Newcastle / York, Leeds and Manchester
You can use the alternative route map to help you with your journey. Please be aware that other operators' services are likely to be busy.
Lumo customer advice:
You may use your ticket to travel on the following services at no extra cost:
• Avanti West Coast services between:
• Edinburgh / Glasgow Central and London Euston via Preston
• Edinburgh / Glasgow Central and Crewe
• LNER services between Newcastle and London Kings Cross
• London Northwestern Railway services between Crewe and London Euston
• Lumo services between Newcastle and London Kings Cross
• Northern services between Newcastle and Morpeth
• ScotRail services between Glasgow Queen Street, Glasgow Central and Edinburgh
• TransPennine Express services between Edinburgh / Glasgow Central and Carlisle. From Carlisle, you can use your ticket to travel on Northern services to Newcastle to connect with services to London Kings Cross via the East Coast Mainline
TransPennine Express customer advice:
You may use your ticket to travel on the following services at no extra cost:
• Alternative TransPennine Express services between Edinburgh and Carlisle
• Avanti West Coast services between Edinburgh and Carlisle
• Northern services between Newcastle and Carlisle
Customers at / for East Linton, Dunbar, Reston, Berwick-upon-Tweed, Alnmouth and Morpeth should see station staff or use station help points where onward travel advice will be provided.
Ticket flexibility:
If your train is cancelled, you will be able to travel on an alternative service operated by any other participating train company, either two hours before or two hours after the original departure time of the cancelled service, in order to reach your destination.
If you decide not to travel or cannot complete your journey due to cancellations, you are entitled to a full refund from your original point of sale.
For further information and guidance please contact your train company or speak to a member of railway staff.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.
For helpful advice if you need to travel on a rail replacement service, including accessibility and bicycle information, please use our Rail Replacement Services page.
You can find the pick-up and drop-off location of rail replacement services by checking station signage or by searching for your station on our Find a Station page.
Please be advised that replacement vehicles may be busier than usual, and you should allow extra time for your journey.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.
